text.title: Competitive Analysis (UX) Procedure
text.summary: 5-step procedure to apply the Competitive Analysis (UX) methodology end-to-end, with step 3 expanded into the six-step analysis run (scope, criteria, hands-on use, documentation, patterns, recommendations).

step.name: check-preconditions
step.input: The "Applies If" + "Skip If" lists from AGENTS.md.
step.action: Verify every Applies-If item holds AND no Skip-If item triggers.
step.output: Boolean: methodology applies / does not apply.
step.decision-gate: If preconditions fail, emit a skip-record naming the failed precondition and STOP.

step.name: gather-inputs
step.action: Read each input; attach its path/URL to the working artefact. Refuse to proceed if any input is unreachable.
step.decision-gate: If any input is unreachable, halt and request the source before proceeding.

step.name: apply-rules
step.input: Inputs gathered + the rules from content/01-core-rules.xml.
step.action: Walk each rule in order; record per-rule pass/fail; capture the violating snippet on any fail.
step.decision-gate: If any HARD rule fails, repair the artefact or escalate; do not return a partially-conformant output.

step.name: produce-artefact
step.input: Rule-conformant inputs + the schema in content/02-output-contract.xml.
step.action: Fill the template under `templates/competitive-analysis.json` according to the schema.

step.name: validate-and-handover
step.action: Run `scripts/validate-competitive-analysis.py --file <path>`. Fix any reported violations. Send to named owner for sign-off.
step.output: Owner-signed artefact registered with the downstream consumer.
step.decision-gate: If validator returns non-zero, do not hand over — repair and re-validate.

step.name: define-scope-and-competitors
step.action: Select the mix per r1-competitor-mix, capped at 8. Competitor types: Direct (same problem, same user — e.g. Uber vs Lyft). Indirect (same problem, different approach — e.g. Uber vs public transit). Partial (overlapping features). Aspirational (best-in-class to learn from, not a competitor). Fill templates/analysis-plan.md.

step.name: define-criteria
step.action: Lock criteria before examining any product (r2-pre-declared-criteria). Dimensions to consider: features (what can users do), user flows (how users accomplish goals), UI patterns (design conventions used), information architecture (content organization), content and tone, accessibility compliance.
step.decision-gate: Any criterion added after examination starts is logged as a separate post-hoc analysis, not merged.

step.name: use-the-products
step.action: Create real accounts and run the flows (r4-account-verified). Data collection: use on both desktop and mobile, complete key user flows end-to-end, document edge cases, contact support, test accessibility.
step.output: Screenshots, recordings, session notes per competitor.

step.name: document-consistently
step.action: Fill templates/competitor-profile.md for each competitor and templates/feature-matrix.md across all (r6-consistent-documentation); cite a screenshot or recording per finding (r5-citation-per-finding).

step.name: analyze-patterns
step.action: Derive baseline, opportunity gap, best practice, and anti-patterns per r7-cross-competitor-patterns.

step.name: prioritized-recommendations
step.action: Tier every recommendation Must / Should / Could / Avoid (r3-mscw-classified); fill templates/summary-report.md.
